protocol: Select -> Segment -> Label functions -> Compare -> Generalize -> Validate -> Version

sources.reason: theory-first introduction with numbered hypotheses tested in Results order
merged Results and Discussion; interventional design with causal language
short conceptual abstract; exploratory analyses labeled; extended discussion
numbered IMRaD with separate Limitations, Implications, Conclusions; three-experiment replication structure

functions.name: state the finding, phenomenon, or characterization in ten to fifteen words
exceptions: declarative-claim form used only with an interventional design

functions.name: signal design strength only when the design supports it
exceptions: observational papers use noun or gerund phrases without causal words

functions.name: establish context in one or two sentences
state the unresolved question with a contrast marker
exceptions: theory-driven summary states the approach immediately after context

functions.name: state what this study did, marking the present study with a locative opener
report specific directional findings naming which system did what
exceptions: numbers, n, and latencies appear only in the long methods-focused abstract

functions.name: close with a synthesizing conclusion and an implication
exceptions: implication sentence is explicit only in the methods-focused abstract

functions.name: four one-line findings and a third-person blurb
open with a concrete readable sentence about the phenomenon, not a universal importance claim
synthesize prior work by idea with grouped citations
frame the unresolved issue as competing accounts or a limitation of prior methods
state the present study's aim, approach, and explicit predictions
exceptions: numbered hypotheses in two papers; conditional if-then predictions in one

functions.name: propose a unified theory with a schematic before testing it
exceptions: only when the materials contain a theory of that scope

functions.name: participants: recruitment, screening, exclusions with reasons, final n with demographics, ethics, consent, safety guidelines
exceptions: reanalysis paper points to source-dataset papers

functions.name: chronological procedure with timings, trial counts, counterbalancing
acquisition parameters inline with equipment, model, coordinates, targeting
ordered preprocessing steps with software versions, thresholds, rejection counts, and code links
analysis: measure definitions, model specification, tests with assumption checks and corrections, exploratory labels, rationale for non-obvious choices
structured methods block with key resources table and availability statements
exceptions: Cell Press venues only; others use conventional Methods after Discussion

functions.name: one subsection per figure or experiment; headers state claims or precise analysis names; order follows hypotheses
exceptions: short report has no subsection headers

functions.name: orienting first paragraph with design recap, behavioral sanity checks, and pointers to Methods
paragraph anatomy: aim, approach, result with inline statistics and figure callout, one-sentence takeaway
inline statistics with test statistic, degrees of freedom, p, effect size, correction; null results reported with equal completeness
exceptions: effect sizes omitted in some correlational reports

functions.name: control analysis after each primary result; replication reported as replication; exploratory analyses labeled
open with a findings-summary paragraph at Results strength, often enumerated
exceptions: merged short report summarizes in the closing paragraphs

functions.name: relate to prior work as replicated, extended, or not replicated with the specific design difference
state alternatives and what cannot be ruled out, paired with the test that would resolve it
limitations as four-part units: limitation, consequence for which claim, mitigation, future work
exceptions: separate numbered Limitations section in one venue; folded elsewhere

functions.name: implications stated conditionally for design and interpretation
close with a bounded conclusion paragraph or short section
first-person plural voice; past tense for actions and findings, present tense for what evidence shows and for established knowledge
concrete opening sentence: aphorism, analogy, lab-versus-life contrast, or technique definition
exceptions: short report opens directly on the construct

functions.name: contrast pivot at paragraph end naming what remains unresolved
unresolved question stated as a closed set of alternatives, often three, with conditional predictions before the design
one rhetorical question at a pivot, answered immediately
question-driven paragraph openers in Results echoing hypothesis numbering
reasoning stated before the result as an if-then sentence
design-affordance sentence explaining why the method earns the inference
effects reported with direction attached via 'such that' and decomposed via 'driven by'
parallel syntactic frames across analogous results
null results with statistics and numerical direction, followed by a consequence sentence
pre-emptive control sentence naming the alternative, testing it, and reporting in the same paragraph
bridging restatement in plain terms for unfamiliar statistics or designs
summative closer at the end of every Results paragraph, hedged to the design
replicate, extend, or fail-to-replicate verbs placing findings in the literature with the explaining design difference
alternative account raised in its own sentence, then tested or bounded, then paired with the resolving experiment
scope disclaimers drawing the claim boundary in the authors' words
multi-line evidence chain enumerated First, Second, Third, Finally
one calibrated priority claim per paper, only where the design earns it
big-picture closing paragraph stating a principle with a modal verb
exceptions: methods-focused paper closes on implications for study design

functions.name: attention markers rationed to one to three per section
rationale voice in Methods and candor about control weaknesses
title sentence, panel-by-panel description, error-bar definition, n, significance markers, supplementary cross-references

validation_note: Functions labeled high were checked across all four sources; cross-source agreement was used as the validation set because no held-out paper was supplied. No paragraph text, phrases, claims, or citations from the sources are stored.
